title: Multi-GPU orchestrator for synchronized prefill/decode scheduling and NCCL overlap
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: On multi-GPU servings we see poor NCCL overlap during mixed prefill + decode workloads. Prefill phases create large collective traffic (AllGather/AllReduce for KV cache and attention states) and are currently scheduled in ways that block low-latency decode tokens. This causes both higher tail latency for interactive requests and suboptimal GPU utilization across pipeline/tensor partitions.

Goal: Implement a runtime orchestration layer that coordinates tensor/pipeline parallel scheduling to maximize NCCL overlap with local compute, prioritize latency-sensitive decode work, and enable safe prefill backgrounding where possible. The orchestrator should be feature-flagged, observable, and fall back to current behavior when disabled.

Constraints: Backwards compatibility with existing model sharding configs, minimal changes to model artifacts, support both pipeline+tensor hybrid topologies, and work with current kernel selector and stream semantics. Must not require privileged NCCL changes on customer clusters.

Success metrics (initial):
- 20-40% increase in tokens/sec for large-batch prefill-heavy workloads on 8-GPU slices
- 10-20% reduction in p95 latency for mixed interactive workloads
- No >1% increase in error rate or memory headroom regressions
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a new runtime.mgpu_orchestrator feature flag that defaults off
Scheduler can reorder prefill micro-batches to overlap NCCL collectives with compute on other stages
Decode-side prioritization: low-latency in-flight tokens are scheduled ahead of background prefill work
Automated perf harness shows target improvements on CI perf cluster (links in benchmarks)
Rollout plan with canary and rollback (console flag + telemetry gating)
tasks: Design proto: sequence diagram for prefill/decode overlap and stream assignment
Implement schedule abstraction that understands pipeline stage dependencies and tensor ranks
Add NCCL-aware micro-batching: mark collectives and enable reordering to hide latency
Make kernel selector stream-aware so compute kernels can be bound to dedicated CUDA streams with pinned priorities
Implement decode preemption: lightweight preemptible prefill tasks + priority queue
Integrate telemetry: per-token latency breakdown, NCCL wait time, GPU occupancy
Create end-to-end tests in perf-harness and run on 4/8 GPU CI nodes
Doc + rollout: confluence design, runtime flags, console rollout controls
design_notes: We will model two scheduling primitives: 'micro-slice' (small contiguous token ranges of prefill) and 'priority token' (decode tokens that must be released asap).
Use CUDA stream priorities: high-priority stream for decode compute, medium for collectives that should overlap, low for background prefill transfers.
Leverage NCCL stream scheduling (enqueue collectives on non-blocking streams) to permit compute/comm overlap; avoid requiring proprietary NCCL ops.
Kernel selector changes: add metadata tag 'stream_affinity' to kernels and choose kernels that are safe to run concurrently when overlapping with NCCL.
Fallback: when topology doesn't support overlap (eg. old drivers or single-stream NCCL), orchestrator falls back to conservative sequential scheduling.
Memory safety: prefetch KV cache shards with staged transfers so that memory spikes are bounded; maintain per-GPU reservation budget.
Trade-offs: more aggressive overlap increases complexity of debugging and may expose subtle race conditions; we will gate with strict assertions and observability during canary.
Interaction with batching: dynamic batching must expose its micro-batches to the orchestrator; consider minimal API extension on the batcher to provide 'micro-batch boundaries'
benchmarks: Baseline cluster: 8x A100 v4, pipeline-2 tensor-4 hybrid model (1B parameters) - baseline tokens/sec: 24k
Target after orchestrator: >= 32k tokens/sec (30% uplift) for prefill-heavy 64-token batch loads
Target p95 latency reduction for mixed workload: 15%
